chief_complaint: swollen knee, heel pain, and painful urination
hpi_details: 32M presents with a very swollen, painful left knee and right heel pain (Achilles tendon area). He also reports painful urination and redness in his left eye starting a week ago. He recently recovered from a severe diarrheal illness.

core_concepts: Classic triad (often incomplete): Urethritis, Conjunctivitis, Arthritis ('Can't see, can't pee, can't climb a tree').
Typically follows a GI (Salmonella/Campylobacter) or GU (Chlamydia) infection.
common_misconceptions: Thinking antibiotics will cure the arthritis (it's an autoimmune reaction, not an active joint infection).
dangerous_errors: Failing to test for Chlamydia in a young sexually active patient with these symptoms.
management_principles: Urgently aspirate an acutely swollen joint to exclude septic arthritis before treating it as reactive arthritis. Test for Chlamydia and gonorrhea and treat proven active infection per local guidance; use NSAIDs only after renal, gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, anticoagulant, and pregnancy-risk review. Same-day ophthalmology assessment is needed for a painful, photophobic red eye or visual symptoms suggestive of uveitis.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: American College of Rheumatology (ACR) Clinical Guidance

reference_soap.subjective: 32M with asymmetric oligoarthritis, enthesitis, dysuria, and conjunctivitis following a GI illness.
reference_soap.objective: Large left knee effusion. Tender right Achilles insertion. Conjunctival injection.
reference_soap.plan: Perform urgent arthrocentesis with synovial studies to exclude septic arthritis. Obtain urine NAAT for chlamydia/gonorrhea and treat any confirmed infection. Use an NSAID only if appropriate after contraindication review; arrange same-day ophthalmology assessment if eye pain, photophobia, or visual change is present.

learning_objectives: Recognize the classic triad and triggers of reactive arthritis.

teaching.one_liner: Asymmetric arthritis, urethritis, and conjunctivitis following a recent GI or GU infection.

must_ask.say: Did you have diarrhea or a stomach illness in the weeks before this started?
Which joints are swollen and painful — is it just the knee and heel?
Have you had any burning or pain when you urinate?
Have you had eye redness with pain, light sensitivity, or any change in vision?
Have you had any new sexual partners recently?

history.answer: My left knee has swollen up terribly and hurts, and the back of my right heel is also aching.
It is mostly my left knee and my right heel; my other knee and joints feel completely fine.
The knee swelling and heel pain began about five days ago and worsened over the next two days.
My knee feels like a severe, tight throbbing ache around a seven out of ten, while the heel is a sharp pain whenever I step on it.
Yes, the left knee is puffy and noticeably warm, though it doesn't look bright red.
Both my knee and heel feel stiff when I get out of bed, and it takes nearly an hour for them to loosen up.
Resting takes the edge off, but bending the knee or walking makes the pain much worse.
I have a pronounced limp and can barely put weight on my left leg, so climbing stairs is very difficult.
No, I haven't had high fevers, night sweats, or shaking chills.
I didn't twist or pop anything, and the knee hasn't caught or locked up; I wondered if I strained it exercising, but there was no specific injury.
No, I have never had a swollen joint or heel pain like this before.
I have felt a little more tired than usual this week, but I haven't lost weight.
My left eye became red and felt slightly gritty about a week ago, but I don't have any rash, hair loss, or dry mouth.
My right Achilles tendon aches intensely where it attaches to the heel, but my lower back and toes feel fine.
About three weeks ago, I had severe watery diarrhea and abdominal cramps for four days after eating out.
For the past week, I have had a burning sensation when I urinate, but I haven't seen any pus or discharge.
No, I don't drink heavily, eat lots of red meat or seafood, or take any water pills.
No, I have never received joint injections, taken steroids, or had any joint surgery.
I am sexually active with a regular long-term partner and have not had new or casual sexual encounters.
I assumed it was a sports injury, but the swelling has me worried, and I was hoping you could drain the fluid today.
I have no history of chronic health problems or joint diseases.
I have never undergone surgery and have never been hospitalized.
I am not currently taking any prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, or supplements.
I do not have any known allergies to medicines.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used tobacco products.
I only drink one or two beers on occasion during social gatherings.
I work as an IT software analyst and live in an apartment with my partner.
There is no family history of rheumatoid arthritis, gout, psoriasis, or spine problems.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 122/78 mmHg, pulse 76 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, temperature 37.1°C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Conjunctival injection of the left eye without purulent discharge or scleral icterus.
Large effusion, increased warmth, and marked tenderness of the left knee with painfully restricted flexion, accompanied by localized tenderness over the right Achilles tendon insertion.
Antalgic gait favoring the left leg with difficulty bearing full weight.
No psoriatic plaques, dactylitis, tophi, keratoderma blennorrhagica, or nail pitting noted.
Normal external male genitalia without circinate balanitis, lesions, or active urethral discharge.
Full active spine range of motion without midline tenderness or pain over the sacroiliac joints.
Oral mucosa is moist and pink without aphthous ulcers or pharyngeal inflammation.
